question.text: <math><mtext>K</mtext><mtext>M</mtext><mtext>n</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> reacts with <math><mtext>KI</mtext></math>, in basic medium to form <math><msub><mrow><mtext>I</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> and <math><mtext>M</mtext><mtext>n</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> . When 250 mL of 0.1 M <math><mtext>K</mtext><mtext>I</mtext></math> solution is mtextxed with 250 mL of 0.02 M <math><mtext>K</mtext><mtext>M</mtext><mtext>n</mtext><msub><mrow><mtext>O</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>4</mn></mrow></msub></math> in basic medium, what is the number of moles of <math><msub><mrow><mtext>I</mtext></mrow><mrow><mn>2</mn></mrow></msub></math> formed?

solution.text:
Number of mtextlli equivalents of MnO4-=0.02×3×250=15

Number of mtextlli equivalents of l2=0.1×1×250=25

Thus, here MnO4- is limtextting reagent.

∴ Number of mtextlli equivalents of l2 formed = Number of mtextlli equivalent of MnO4-=15

Or number of equivalent of l2 formed =151000=0.015

∴ Number of moles of l2 formed =0.0152

=0.0075
